learning_outcomes.text: Define clinical decision support (CDS) and its goals as an educational concept
Describe rule-based and model-based CDS approaches and alerts
Explain how CDS integrates with clinical workflow and electronic records
Explain why CDS augments and does not replace clinician judgement, requiring confirmation
Identify risks such as alert fatigue, automation bias and inequity
Summarise evaluation, governance and safety principles for CDS systems

integrative_case: A clinical-informatics student reviews, as an educational case, a decision-support alert that fires too often; they explain how alert fatigue and automation bias arise, propose how to measure the tool's impact, and state that final decisions remain with the confirming clinician.
assesses: knowledge and applied reasoning on every in-scope outcome via MCQ/MR
case-based decisions in the integrative case
